summary:
“Lost But Not Forgotten” is a research project focused on objects left behind on the Moon during NASA space missions. It explores the history of Apollo 11, Apollo 12, Apollo 15, and Surveyor 3, investigating the objects that remained on the lunar surface, their purpose, and the circumstances surrounding each mission.

The main goal is to preserve and share this lesser-known part of space exploration through an interactive website featuring a 3D model of the Moon. Visitors will be able to explore the landing sites, identify their locations, and learn about the objects left behind.

The research is based on NASA publications, historical records, photographs, and other reliable sources. By combining historical information with interactive technology, the project aims to make space exploration more accessible and interesting, while showing that even objects left behind have a story worth remembering.
details:
Our project is about researching objects left on the Moon during NASA missions, focusing on Apollo 11, Apollo 12, Apollo 15, and Surveyor 3.

How does it work?
We created an interactive website with a 3D Moon model. Visitors can explore the landing sites and click on specific locations to discover information about the missions and the objects that remained there.

What are its benefits?
It makes learning about space exploration more interesting, accessible, and interactive. It also helps preserve an important part of space history.

Expected impact:
We hope to encourage students and visitors to become more interested in science, technology, and space exploration.

Tools and software:
We used ChatGPT and Google AI Studio as support during development, along with web development technologies to create the website and its 3D Moon model.

What makes it creative?
Instead of presenting information only through text, our project allows users to explore the Moon and discover its history through an interactive experience.

Factors considered:
We considered historical accuracy, reliable information, landing locations, ease of use, and the importance of making the website understandable for everyone.
